parsed.explanation: No trans-specific criminalisation, no documented facility, custody, border or care restriction, and same-sex conduct has been lawful since 1933 — so there is no tier-1 or tier-2 state exposure. Against that: the 2007 hate-speech/hate-crime provision lists sexual orientation but not gender identity, so a trans visitor has no clear statutory recourse; the political class has a documented decade of hostility to LGBT public expression (2010 banquet refusal, 2015 attacks on the broadcaster and drag show, Pride-ban demands); and the only recorded violence against gender-nonconforming visitors — a visiting drag group chased in 2005 and a gay performer beaten in 2006 — is visitor-facing but dated two decades, so weak evidence either way. Zero trans-specific documentation in a jurisdiction with moderate LGBT coverage leaves acceptance unproven; there is no third-gender tradition or protective machinery to credit. Extrapolating from the LGB-only protection gap, recorded political hostility and unmeasured police practice, it sits a step below the acceptance-with-working-remedies tier.
